verses.sanskrit:
अकृतव्रण उवाच।
              दुःखद्वयमिदं भद्रे कतरस्य चिकीर्षसि। प्रतिकर्तव्यमबले तत्त्वं वत्से वदस्व मे ॥१॥
verses.english: Akritavrana said For which of these two sorrows do you desire a remedy, O lady. Tell me that truly, 0 child.

verses.sanskrit: यदि सौभपतिर्भद्रे नियोक्तव्यो मतस्तव। नियोक्ष्यति महात्मा स रामस्त्वद्धितकाम्यया ॥२॥
verses.english: If in your opinion gentle lady, the lord of the Suabhas should be urged, the great-souled Rama, desirous of your good, will urge him.
verses.bhavadeepa: दुःखद्वयमिति । दुःखद्वयं दुःखकरद्वयं, भीष्मशाल्वाख्यं यद्वा । निर्भर्तृकत्वमेकं दुःखं त्वच्छत्रोर्वधश्चेति तापसानां दुःखद्वयं तथाऽपि शत्रुद्वयमध्ये कतरस्य कं प्रतिकर्तव्यं हन्तुं यत्नं चिकीर्षसि । यद्वा । एकैकस्य गतिहानिर्मरणं वेति दुःखद्वयं ज्ञेयम् ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: अथापगेयं भीष्मं त्वं रामेणेच्छसि धीमता। रणे विनिर्जितं द्रष्टुं कुर्यात्तदपि भार्गवः ॥३॥
verses.english: Or if you desire to see the blamable Bhishma vanquished in battle by the wise Rama, he, of Bhrigu's family, will do that too.

verses.sanskrit: सृञ्जयस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तव चैव शुचिस्मिते। यदत्र ते भृशं कार्यं तदद्यैव विचिन्त्यताम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Hearing the words of Srinjaya, and of yours, O you of beautiful smiles, let what ought to be done this very day be settled.
verses.bhavadeepa: भीष्मस्य तु सत्यप्रतिज्ञस्य त्वत्सुखार्थं जयमात्रं कर्तव्यं न तु तावता तव हितमित्याशयेनाह - अथेति॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: अम्बोवाच। अपनीताऽस्मि भीष्मेण भगवन्नविजानता। नाभिजानाति मे भीष्मो ब्रह्मन् शाल्वगतं मनः ॥५॥
verses.english: Amba said Led away I had been by Bhishma, but he knew not the true state of my feelings. Bhishma did not know, O Brahmana, that my mind learned towards Shalva.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्विचार्य मनसा भवानेतद्विनिश्चयम्। विचिनोतु यथान्यायं विधानं क्रियतां तथा ॥६॥
verses.english: Thinking of this in your mind you should settle about this; do what you think is just.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मे वा कुरुशार्दूले शाल्वराजेऽथवा पुनः। उभयोरेव वा ब्रह्मन् युक्तं यत्तत् समाचर ॥७॥
verses.english: Do that wish is just and reasonable towards that best among the Kurus and to the king Shalva or to both.

verses.sanskrit: निवेदितं मया ह्येतद्दुःखमूलं यथातथम्। विधानं तत्र भगवन् कर्तुमर्हसि युक्तितः ॥८॥
verses.english: The root of my distress, as it is, had now been submitted by me and it is proper that you should do in this matte what is reasonable.

verses.sanskrit:
अकृतव्रण उवाच।
              उपपन्नमिदं भद्रे यदेवं वरवर्णिनि। धर्मं प्रति वचो ब्रूयाः शृणु चेदं वचो मम ॥९॥
verses.english: Akritavrana said It is indeed praiseworthy, gentle lady, that you are speaking these words with your eye towards virtue, O you of fair complexion; listen to these words of mine.

verses.sanskrit: यदि त्वामापगेयो वै न नयेद्गजसाह्वयम्। शाल्वस्त्वां शिरसा भीरु गृह्णीयाद्रामचोदितः ॥१०॥
verses.english: If the blamable one had not led you to the city called after the elephant, Shalva would have accepted you, O timid lady, with his head bowed down, urged by Rama.

verses.sanskrit: तेन त्वं निर्जिता भद्रे यस्मान्नीताऽसि भाविनि। संशयः शाल्वराजस्य तेन त्वयि सुमध्यमे ॥११॥
verses.english: But since you, gentle lady, had been taken away by him after gaining a victory, O romantic lady, the king Shalva has therefore doubts in you, o you of beautiful waist.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मः पुरुषमानी च जितकाशी तथैव च। तस्मात् प्रतिक्रिया युक्ता भीष्मे कारयितुं तव ॥१२॥
verses.english: Bhishma is proud of his bravery and success and therefore it stands to reason that your remedy lies in Bhishma.

verses.sanskrit: अम्बोवाच। ममाप्येष सदा ब्रह्मन् हृदि कामोऽभिवर्तते। घातयेयं यदि रणे भीष्ममित्येव नित्यदा ॥१३॥
verses.english: Amba said This desire has ever obtained in my heart. O Brahmana, that I would have but Bhishma slain in battle.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मं वा शाल्वराजं वा यं वा दोषेण गच्छसि। प्रशाधि तं महाबाहो यत्कृतेऽहं सुदुःखिता ॥१४॥
verses.english: Whoever is blamable, Bhishma to the king of the Shalvas, punish him who has brought about this great distress, O you of long arms.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एवं कथयतामेव तेषां स दिवसो गतः। रात्रिश्च भरतश्रेष्ठ सुखशीतोष्णमारुता ॥१५॥
verses.english: Bhishma said The day passed away while they were conversing on this as also the night which was marked by pleasant breezes that were neither too hot nor too cold, O chief among the Bharatas.

verses.sanskrit: ततो रामः प्रादुरासीत् प्रज्ज्वलन्निव तेजसा। शिष्यैः परिवृतो राजन् जटाचीरधरो मुनिः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Then did Rama come there as if blazing with energy, the anchorite having matted hairs wearing deer skin was surrounded by his disciples.

verses.sanskrit: धनुष्पाणिरदीनात्मा खड्गं बिभ्रत् परश्वधी। विरजा राजशार्दूल सृञ्जयं सोऽभ्ययान्नृपम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: The great-souled one came, bow in hand, and holding a sword and battle-axe; and the sinless one approached that ruler of men, Srinjaya, O best among kings.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तं तापसा दृष्ट्वा स च राजा महातपाः। तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयो राजन् सा च कन्या तपस्विनी ॥१८॥
verses.english: Seeing him the ascetics and the king of great asceticism stood up with clasped hands; so also did that girl.

verses.sanskrit: पूजयामासुरव्यग्रा मधुपर्केण भार्गवम्। अर्चितश्च यथान्यायं निषसाद सहैव तैः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Earnestly they adored him of the Bhrigu race, with honey and curds and being duly honored he sat down with them.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पूर्वव्यतीतानि कथयन्तौ स्म तावुभौ। आसातां जामदग्न्यश्च सृञ्जयश्चैव भारत ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then the two Srinjaya and the son of Jamadagna, sat together conversing on past matters.

verses.sanskrit: तथा कथान्ते राजर्षिर्भृगुश्रेष्ठं महाबलम्। उवाच मधुरं काले रामं वचनमर्थवत् ॥२१॥
verses.english: At the end of their discourse, the royal sage in proper time said these sweet words pregnant with meaning to Rama, the foremost in the race of Bhrigu, endued with great strength.

verses.sanskrit: रामेयं मम दौहित्री काशिराजसुता प्रभो। अस्याः शृणु यथातत्त्वं कार्यं कार्यविशारद ॥२२॥
verses.english: O Rama this is my grand daughter, the daughter of the king of the Kashis, my lord; hear what she has to say and settle what can be done for her, O you skillful in deeds.

verses.sanskrit: परमं कथ्यतां चेति तां रामः प्रत्यभाषत। ततः साऽभ्यवदद्रामं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Rama said to her, “Repeat your grand story"; thereupon she said to Rama who was blazing like fire.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभिवाद्य चरणौ रामस्य शिरसौ शुभौ। स्पृष्ट्वा पद्मतलाभाभ्यां पाणिभ्यामग्रतः स्थिता ॥२४॥
verses.english: Saluting the holy feet of Rama with her head she touched them with her lotus like hands and stood in front of him.

verses.sanskrit: रुरोद सा शोकवती बाष्पव्याकुललोचना। प्रपेदे शरणं चैव शरण्यं भृगुनन्दनम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: Being stricken with grief she wept aloud and with her eyes bathed in tears she betook herself to the refuge of the delighter of Bhrigu's race who was of a worthy refuge.
verses.bhavadeepa: शिरसौ श्रेष्ठौ । ‘शिरः प्रधाने सेनाग्रे’ इति मेदिनी । पुंस्त्वमार्षम् ॥२४॥

verses.sanskrit:
राम उवाच।
              यथा त्वं सृञ्जयस्यास्य तथा मे त्वं नृपात्मजे। ब्रूहि यत्ते मनोदुःखं करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥२६॥
verses.english: Rama said You are the same to me, O princess, as you are to Srinjaya; speak out the grief you have in your mind, I shall act up to your words.

verses.sanskrit: अम्बोवाच। भगवन् शरणं त्वाऽद्य प्रपन्नाऽस्मि महाव्रतम्। शोकपङ्कार्णवान्मग्नां घोरादुद्धर मां विभो ॥२७॥
verses.english: Amba said My lord, I be take myself now to your refuge for you are of great vows, Tell me, my lord, who am fallen into the mire of grief and liberate me from the heavy calamity.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              तस्याश्च दृष्ट्वा रूपं च वपुश्चाभिनवं पुनः। सौकुमार्यं परं चैव रामश्चिन्तापरोऽभवत् ॥२८॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Seeing her beauty and again her youthful person and her extreme delicacy of mold, Rama became engaged in deep thought.

verses.sanskrit: किमियं वक्ष्यतीत्येवं विममर्श भृगूद्वहः। इति दध्यौ चिरं रामः कृपयाऽभिपरिप्लुतः ॥२९॥
verses.english: "What shall this one say?" So thought Bhrigu; thinking thus Rama was silent for a long time filled with pity.

verses.sanskrit: कथ्यतामिति सा भूयो रामेणोक्ता शुचिस्मिता। सर्वमेव यथातत्त्वं कथयामास भार्गवे ॥३०॥
verses.english: The lady, of sweet smiles being again asked to recite her story, said everything as had happened to him of Bhrigu's race.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा जामदग्न्यस्तु राजपुत्र्या वचस्तदा। उवाच तां वरारोहां निश्चित्यार्थविनिश्चयम् ॥३१॥
verses.english: The son of Jamadagni too hearing those words of the princess first settled as to what he should do and then said to her of beautiful hips.

verses.sanskrit:
राम उवाच।
              प्रेषयिष्यामि भीष्माय कुरुश्रेष्ठाय भाविनि। करिष्यति वचो मह्यं श्रुत्वा च स नराधिपः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Rama said O beautiful lady, I shall send words to that foremost among the Kurus, Bhishma, and that ruler among men. Hearing them will do, my bidding.

verses.sanskrit: न चेत्करिष्यति वचो मयोक्तं जाह्नवीसुतः। धक्ष्याम्यहं रणे भद्रे सामात्यं शस्त्रतेजसा ॥३३॥
verses.english: If the son of Jahnavi does not do what I say then shall I consume him in battle, O gentle lady, along with his ministers, by the blaze of my weapons.

verses.sanskrit: अथवा ते मतिस्तत्र राजपुत्रि न वर्तते। यावच्छाल्वपतिं वीरं योजयाम्यत्र कर्मणि ॥३४॥
verses.english: If, O princess, you are not of that opinion, I shall urge that hero, the king of the Shalvas, to the present matter.

verses.sanskrit: अम्बोवाच। विसर्जिताऽहं भीष्मेण श्रुत्वैव भृगुनन्दन। शाल्वराजगतं भावं मम पूर्वं मनीषितम् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Amba said O delighter of Bhrigu's race, I had been dismissed by Bhishma as soon as he heard that my mind already had been to the king of the Shalvas.

verses.sanskrit: सौभराजमुपेत्याहमवोचं दुर्वचं वचः। न च मां प्रत्यगृह्णात् स चारित्र्यपरिशङ्कितः ॥३६॥
verses.english: Approaching then the king of Saubha I addressed him in improper words, but he did not accept me being suspicious of my character.

verses.sanskrit: एतत् सर्वं विनिश्चित्य स्वबुद्ध्या भृगुनन्दन। यदत्रौपयिकं कार्यं तच्चिन्तयितुमर्हसि ॥३७॥
verses.english: Thinking on all this, it is proper should think of the means of remedying this by your own knowledge, O delighter of Bhrigu's that you race.

verses.sanskrit: मम तु व्यसनस्यास्य भीष्मो मूलं महाव्रतः। येनाहं वशमानीता समुत्क्षिप्य बलात्तदा ॥३८॥
verses.english: The root of this distress of mine is Bhishma of great vows, since by him was I brought under subjection taking me up by force.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मं जहि महाबाहो यत्कृते दुःखमीदृशम्। प्राप्ताऽहं भृगुशार्दूल चराम्यप्रियमुत्तमम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: Slay Bhishma, O you of long arms, for it is by his doings that I am fallen into such distress, O you foremost among the race of Bhrigu, and that I continue in this growing distress.

verses.sanskrit: स हि लुब्धश्च नीचश्च जितकाशी च भार्गव। तस्मात् प्रतिक्रिया कर्तुं युक्ता तस्मै त्वयाऽनघ ॥४०॥
verses.english: He is covetous, mean, spirited, and boastful of success, O you of Bhrigu's race; therefore is it reasonable that you should take revenge on him, O sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: एष मे क्रियमाणाया भारतेन तदा विभो। अभवद्धृदि संकल्पो घातयेयं महाव्रतम् ॥४१॥
verses.english: When I was being taken away by Bharata, my lord, I made this resolution in my heart, namely, that I should cause this one of great vows to be slain.
verses.bhavadeepa: लुब्धो यतो मां हृतवान् । नीचो यतो मदङ्गीकारं स्वयं न कृतवान् । अकामुकस्य कन्याहरणं दोष इति भावः ॥४०॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात् कामं ममाद्येमं राम सम्पादयानघ। जहि भीष्मं महाबाहो यथा वृत्रं पुरन्दरः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Therefore do you fulfill this desire of mine, O sinless Rama; slay Bhishma, O you of long arms, as Purandara slew Vritra.
verses.bhavadeepa: क्रियमाणायाः बलादाहरणेन हिंस्यमानायाः। कृ हिंसायां स्वादिः ॥४१॥
